coaching.headline: Kaelen's objective takes and Lt. Belica's damage won the game; three deaths at the third Fangtooth were the leak to fix.

flags.text: Kaelen took three Fangtooths, Genesis Core, Primal Fangtooth and Orb Prime, with a game-high 55460 objective damage.
Lt. Belica was the damn engine: game-high 34342 hero damage and eight kills for a single death.
Murdock closed the game as destroyer of the enemy duo inner, mid inhibitor and Core.
Third Fangtooth, shit trade: Murdock, Dekker, Kaelen died at the pit, then Argus took the allied mid outer.

focus.title: Leave the pit together
focus.action: After each Fangtooth take, Kaelen, Murdock and Dekker leave the pit together and reset unless Argus and Eden are dead; after a won fight, hit structures next, as the final two fights did.

20.3.call: Argus scored two of the three kills around the take, Eden the third. Next Fangtooth: Dekker holds Stasis Bomb to peel for Murdock at the pit.

25.7.call: Won 3-0 in the enemy half and cashed: mid inner, duo inner, duo inhibitor and Primal Fangtooth followed. Repeat that order after any clean fight.

27.8.call: Won 4-0 with Orb Prime taken during the fight; the mid inhibitor and Core fell within the same minute. After a four-kill fight, end on the Core.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Four deaths, all to Eden on the offlane in the allied half, against five kills on Eden. When Eden's Heat builds, disengage until the Heat decays, then punish melee stance.
Eden razed both allied offlane towers, the inner shortly after the fourth death. After any death to Eden, call Kaelen or Lt. Belica to cover the offlane inner.
Hero damage 466 per minute on a 567 norm, despite 10.7 CS per minute on a 9.5 norm. Trade on Eden only after Talon Drive is spent.
f551abbb-1a66-42fa-9b8e-9eb5e05b397b: 910 hero damage per minute on a 700 norm. When pushing the duo lane in the enemy half, track Legion first: one of four deaths came there.
Died first at the third Fangtooth, to Argus at the pit, then to Greystone on mid. Near the pit with Argus unseen, stay behind Kaelen until Dread Nova is spent.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Three kills on other lanes, including Greystone 15 seconds after Dekker fell on the duo lane. Once mid is shoved, keep taking those trips.
One death: Argus on mid, inside the fight lost 1-3 before allied duo outer and offlane inner fell. Once a fight turns, back off until allies respawn.
0a3e96fd-03f1-4a5c-bc99-389132d7ee58: Ten wards and three destroyed against Steel's eight placed, plus 13 assists for 52% kill participation. Before every Fangtooth, hold that ward pace.
Died first in three fights, and once to Argus outside any detected fight on the duo lane. With Argus unseen, ward the duo river before walking up.
d9574baa-4b8a-4749-a608-e7456248846d: Game-high healing at 33128 and game-high mitigation at 58390, for a single death. Open the next teamfight with Frostfall when all five are up.
Two wards placed, fewest of all ten, and the lone death came to Argus at the Fangtooth pit. If wards were equipped, ward the pit approach before each Fangtooth.

matchup: Eden posted the top enemy hero damage, 34056, stacking Scattershot and Sky Splitter on every basic attack.
Eden's melee stance heals from hero damage, on top of 22% lifesteal and Terminus.
The field record for Scarlett into Eden sits at 51.8% across 23 games.
build: Tainted Blade met the anti-heal need: physical damage briefly cuts the target's healing.
Rebirth was finished last, after the final death, so the resurrect never had a death to answer.
Mutilator adds max-health damage on basic attacks and ability hits; Solaris heals off the empowered attack after a cast.
eternal: Marrow heals from hero damage, more at low health; Blood Bank adds lifesteal from stored hero damage.
Knell leans first in the Scarlett offlane field; Marrow ranks behind Knell and Vesh.
Blood Bank with Jealousy is the best Marrow pair; The Maw only adds true damage against low-health targets.
augment: Volcaic Slam leaves a rupture after empowered Cindara that erupts for damage and a slow.
Volcaic Slam is the clear best augment in the Scarlett offlane field. Sound keep.
crest: Judgement's active deals area damage and heals on hero hits.
Iceskorn Talons and Gravitum lead a toss-up in the Scarlett offlane field; Judgement, the most played, ranks behind both.
improvement: Physical armor NOT built while all four deaths came to Eden: 27383 of 28517 hero damage taken was physical.
Citadel in Rebirth's slot trades the resurrect for physical armor while keeping physical power and health.
Terminus and Solaris match the extra buys the field makes into Eden; keep both.

matchup: Duo faced Legion and Steel; duo deaths before minute ten ran one allied to two enemy.
Three kills on Legion, while Legion and Steel each scored a death on the carry.
In the field, Legion wins the lane 55.7% of the time across 457 games.
build: Lightning Hawk and Vanquisher match the most played core into Legion; Imperator, the third piece, was skipped.
Demolisher ignores part of physical armor, a fit into Steel's Forticus and 42980 mitigation.
Sky Splitter, finished last, adds current-health damage on basics; earlier fights ran without Sky Splitter.
eternal: Vermis adds max-health damage on every third straight basic on one hero; Serration adds missing-health damage.
Thraex and Xyris lead a toss-up in the Murdock carry field; Vermis ranks last among options with enough games.
augment: Justice's Reach makes Shots Fired pierce units with extra range.
Justice's Reach is the clear best augment in the Murdock carry field. Sound keep.
crest: Liberator's active cleanses debuffs and grants a short shield.
Pacifier is the clear best crest in the Murdock carry field; Liberator, the most played, ranks well behind.
improvement: Tainted Rounds NOT built against three self-healing kits; Greystone healed 15233.
Tainted Rounds in Sky Splitter's slot cuts healing on basic attacks, trading away the current-health damage.
Pacifier over Liberator is the field-backed swap: a dash and empowered hit, giving up the cleanse.

matchup: Lane opponent was Argus; the field record for the pairing is 48% across 231 games.
Three kills on Argus, all on mid in the enemy half.
None of the four heroes killed built magical armor, so the penetration cut deep.
build: Combustion, Noxia and Wraith Leggings complete the most played core into Argus; Oblivion Crown completes the best overall core too.
Caustica ignores 35% of magical armor, stacking with the flat penetration on Combustion and Wraith Leggings.
Oblivion Crown, finished last, raises magical power by a quarter; earlier fights ran without Oblivion Crown.
eternal: Aion grants mana regeneration on casts and gold from spell damage; Runic Focus scales magical power with current mana.
Lotus leans first in the Lt. Belica mid field; Aion ranks behind Lotus, Xyris and Weald.
Bottomless Vial with Arcane Resonance is the best Aion pair; Bottomless Vial with Runic Focus is the most played.
augment: Combat Veteran adds movement speed and passive experience each second.
Combat Veteran is the clear best augment in the Lt. Belica mid field. Sound keep.
crest: Soulbearer's active grants a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed.
Epoch and Soulbearer lead a toss-up in the Lt. Belica mid field. Sound keep.
improvement: Anti-heal NOT built against Greystone, Eden and Legion, all self-healing kits; Tainted Scepter is the listed answer.
Tainted Scepter in Caustica's slot cuts healing on magical damage, giving up the armor ignore.
Arcane Resonance over Runic Focus matches the best Aion pair: faster basic cooldowns from mana regeneration.

matchup: Duo faced Legion and Steel; Legion scored two of the six deaths on the support.
Steel's Shield Slam knocks up and stuns, the stun to wait out before engaging.
build: Crescelia empowers the next basic after a cast and pays gold on hero hits.
Timewarp and Dynamo, the rest of the most played core into Steel, gave way to Prophecy, Caustica and Megacosm.
Hero damage reached 25908, third among allies, on the damage-leaning build.
eternal: The engine does not model support Eternals; Exarch has too few Dekker support games to lead.
Lotus is the clear best Eternal in the Dekker support field.
augment: Polarity Strike makes Ion Strike also shield allied heroes.
Nothin' But Net leans first in the Dekker support field; Polarity Strike ranks last of three.
crest: Tranquility's active heals nearby heroes and adds brief damage mitigation; crest healing reached 4511.
Tranquility leads a toss-up with Leafsong and Sanctification in the Dekker support field. Sound keep.
improvement: No anti-heal item on the support into three self-healing kits; Tainted Charm or Tainted Totem is the listed answer.
Tainted Charm in Prophecy's slot slows and cuts healing near enemy heroes, giving up basic-attack damage.
Nothin' But Net over Polarity Strike is the field lean: gold and magical power from Stasis Bomb, losing the ally shield.

matchup: Jungle opponent was Greystone; the field record for the pairing is 52.8% across 245 games.
Kills spread across Steel and Legion twice each, plus Greystone and Argus once each.
build: Basilisk and Forticus are two pieces of the best overall core; Tainted Guard, the third piece, was skipped.
Vortex Stone shields and cuts basic cooldowns on immobilizing heroes, a fit with Rimefang, Winter's Pursuit and Frostfall.
Earthshaker stacks ability damage on hits, twice as fast for melee heroes.
eternal: Krix raises max health and size; Regenerative Tissue regenerates health after a stretch without hero damage.
Idrisil is the clear best Eternal in the Kaelen jungle field; Krix ranks behind Idrisil, Nihil and Knell.
Regenerative Tissue with Cannibalism is the best Krix pair; Predator is the most played partner.
augment: Last Winter speeds allies in the Frostfall zone; on landing, Kaelen gains a shield that grows per hero hit.
Last Winter is the clear best augment in the Kaelen jungle field. Sound keep.
crest: Thunder Cleaver, the Judgement active, hits an area and heals off each hero struck at reduced strength after the first.
Nyr Warboots leans first in the Kaelen jungle field; Judgement ranks behind five crests with enough games.
improvement: Missing anti-heal into three self-healing kits; Tainted Guard or Tainted Bastion is the listed answer.
Tainted Guard in Earthshaker's slot cuts the healing of basic attackers and adds armor, losing ability-damage stacks.
Idrisil over Krix is the field pick: bonus armors and a low-health shield instead of extra max health.

synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Dekker) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: First Intent dash in for a shield, Ashen Vow outer edge to slow and empower Cindara, Swan Song to restrain the target and set her blade Ablaze, then Minueta stabs to execute.
ourKits.winCondition: Land Swan Song on a key target to restrain them and spend the Ablaze window with longer range and more power, finishing with Minueta.
ourKits.passive: Last Light: she uses Energy instead of Mana, restores Energy on takedowns, and turns bonus mana into physical power.
ourKits.playWith: Engage or CC teammates who group enemies for Ashen Vow and help her reach the restrained target.
ourKits.playAgainst: Ashen Vow has a short channel and its slow is on the outer edge, so step inside or away. She is Unstoppable during Swan Song, so save CC for after it; fight her after First Intent's shield is spent. Armor answers her physical damage.

ourKits.combo: Root a target with Static Trap, shred armor with Buckshot, stack attack speed with Hot Pursuit and finish with the long-range Charged shot or Long Arm of the Law.
ourKits.winCondition: Control space with traps and out-range enemies with Charged basic attacks, then snipe low targets anywhere with Long Arm of the Law.
ourKits.passive: Shots Fired: after 5 landed basic attacks his next one gains extra range and bonus damage.
ourKits.playWith: A frontline or peeling support, since his only escape tools are Buckshot's push back and Hot Pursuit's speed.
ourKits.playAgainst: Avoid fighting over Static Traps and engage after Buckshot is used, since it is his push-back peel. Stay out of the ult line at low health; armor does not help against Long Arm of the Law.

ourKits.combo: Void Drone for vision and mana drain, Seismic Assault to knock up and stun, Void Bomb, then Neural Disruptor to silence and finish.
ourKits.winCondition: Drain mana with Void Drone and land Seismic Assault, then burst with Neural Disruptor's missing-mana damage.
ourKits.passive: Innovation upgrades each ability at max rank and grants ability haste.
ourKits.playWith: Follow-up damage during Seismic Assault's knockup and stun.
ourKits.playAgainst: Seismic Assault erupts after a short delay, so sidestep the line. Avoid casting near Void Drone since it zaps and drains mana, and dive her after Seismic Assault is used; magical armor helps.

ourKits.combo: Containment Fence traps a target, Stasis Bomb stuns from range, Ion Strike blasts to stun the center and slow the edge, and Photon Disruptor slows
ourKits.winCondition: trap a target in the fence and chain stuns so the team collapses
ourKits.passive: jumping mid-air fires Rocket Boots upward and speeds nearby allies; abilities cut its cooldown
ourKits.playWith: burst that converts her stun and fence into a kill
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Stasis Bomb, whose stun gets longer the farther it travels; step out of the Ion Strike center during its delay; stay out of the fence ring or flank around it; tenacity shortens her stuns

ourKits.combo: Rimefang to stun, slow and lay Rimeglass, Winter's Pursuit onto the Frostbitten target to root them, Razorstorm on Rimeglass, then Frostfall to crash down and root the center.
ourKits.winCondition: Fight on his Rimeglass, where Razorstorm boosts his armor and Frostbite deals max health true damage and sets up Winter's Pursuit roots.
ourKits.passive: Heart of Ice makes his abilities leave Rimeglass that slows and burns enemies with Frostbite.
ourKits.playWith: Damage dealers who can follow up on his roots and Frostfall.
ourKits.playAgainst: Step off Rimeglass so Frostbite ends before Winter's Pursuit can root you. Frostfall channels before he leaps, so move out of the center of the landing and leave the Rimestorm; tenacity helps against the roots.

enemyKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap in, Make Way to shred armor, Sacred Oath empowered cleave to slow, then Stone Forged Soul to heal in Stasis and crash down.
enemyKits.winCondition: Stay in the middle of fights and use Stone Forged Soul's missing-health heal to reset, while Make Way shreds armor for the team.
enemyKits.passive: Stoicism deflects the next basic attack on a cooldown and grants health regen and armor that grow as he loses health.
enemyKits.playWith: Damage dealers who can follow his leap and benefit from Make Way's armor shred.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Do not burst into Stone Forged Soul's Stasis; step away from the slow and the crash, then re-engage. Open with an ability since Stoicism deflects a basic, and buy anti-heal to cut the ult heal.

enemyKits.combo: poke with Sidewind's Railshot and Tachyon Lance at range, swap with Zero Shift, dash in with Talon Drive and Axiom Strike, then Limit Break once Overheated
enemyKits.winCondition: build Heat by damaging heroes and unload Limit Break, flexing between range and melee
enemyKits.passive: damaging heroes builds Heat; at max Heat she Overheats and unlocks Limit Break, and Heat decays if she stops hitting heroes
enemyKits.playWith: peel that lets her keep damaging heroes to build Heat safely
enemyKits.playAgainst: disengage to let her Heat decay before she Overheats; punish melee stance after Talon Drive is spent, and buy anti-heal against her melee stance healing; armor blunts her physical damage

enemyKits.combo: Ether Crystal pushes then implodes to pull enemies together, Dread Nova stuns the group, Particle Shredder homes in, then Synaptic Obliterator beams finish low targets
enemyKits.winCondition: poke from long range, zone with Ether Crystal and land Dread Nova stuns into Obliterator beams
enemyKits.passive: abilities apply Disintegration stacks that make further ability hits deal more damage
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline to protect him while he channels Synaptic Obliterator
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Dread Nova, his only stun; dive him during the Synaptic Obliterator channel when he is immobile, and keep health high since beams hit harder on missing health; magic armor blunts his damage

enemyKits.combo: Bull Rush in unstoppable to knock back → Shield Bash stun → Shield Slam knockup and stun, Force Shield to block projectiles
enemyKits.winCondition: engage with Shield Slam or Bull Rush and protect carries with Force Shield's projectile wall
enemyKits.passive: a self-shield that lasts until broken and refreshes when out of damage, plus hybrid armor
enemyKits.playWith: ranged carries he can shield from enemy projectiles, and follow-up damage for his engages
enemyKits.playAgainst: Bull Rush is unstoppable, so do not waste CC into it; walk around Force Shield instead of shooting into it, and fight after Shield Slam is on cooldown

enemyKits.combo: Saturation Charge mines to slow, Frag Order to launch enemies, Orbital Sanction to track them, Rally Point to knock back divers and heal allies.
enemyKits.winCondition: Hold an area with Orbital Sanction and mines while Rally Point keeps his team healthy and his rifle on infinite ammo.
enemyKits.passive: Ballistic Calibration turns bonus attack speed into ability haste and unlocks ability upgrades at item stat thresholds.
enemyKits.playWith: Frontliners who fight inside Rally Point's heal and hold enemies in the Orbital beam.
enemyKits.playAgainst: Stun him while he cooks Frag Order to make him drop it. Bait Rally Point's knockback before engaging, trade when he reloads, and buy anti-heal against Rally Point's heal and armor against his physical damage.

lines: Lead story: Hard to kill. Died 1 time in 29 minutes, fewer deaths than about 90% of Lt. Belica mid players this patch.
Neural Disruptor at top rank: 85s base, about 70.8s by the end (17% shorter) from 20 ability haste: Noxia 20.
Lt. Belica dealt 34,342 hero damage, 28% of their team's, with +470 magical power from items.

Penetration: Combustion 9, Wraith Leggings 11, Caustica ignores 35%; against Argus (level 15 estimated: about 44 magical armor, 9 after penetration) and Eden (level 15 estimated: about 40 magical armor, 6 after penetration) that is about 33% and 32% more damage (estimate: percent penetration taken before flat).
Combustion (item): On dealing Ability Damage: Deal 50 (+18%) Damage to the Target and nearby Enemies.
Wraith Leggings (item): Against Heroes below 40% Health: Abilities deal 12% bonus Magical Damage.
Noxia (item): Deal 6% of Target's Maximum Health as bonus Damage.
Caustica (item): On dealing Ability Damage to a Hero: While they are above 50% Health. For every point of Bonus Magical Armor they possess. Deal 0.2% more Damage.

Lesson: Lt. Belica's penetration cut through: Argus took about 33% more magical damage than their armor alone allows (estimate: at level 15 (estimated) their armor was about 44, about 9 after 20 flat + 35% penetration).

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 4 effects on one trigger: Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Noxia, Caustica. Lt. Belica has 4 damaging abilities (Void Bomb, Seismic Assault, Void Drone hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 20 ability haste brought them back 17% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Countered? 0 of the 4 players Lt. Belica killed built magical armor. Anti-heal on Steel. We killed Lt. Belica 1 time.

bullets: Every basic attack set off both Scattershot and Sky Splitter, so Eden's fast shots added a slice of the target's current health to each hit.
Scattershot fires 2 extra projectiles toward the closest enemies that carry on-hit effects at 50% strength, spreading Sky Splitter's health damage beyond the main target.
Terminus and Sky Splitter healed Eden off damage dealt, and melee stance returned a share of hero damage as more health when Eden switched in close.
Each ability hit could set off Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Noxia and Caustica, so Void Bomb, Seismic Assault and drone zaps stacked extra item damage.
Void Bomb and Seismic Assault hit every enemy in the area, so one cast spread Combustion's splash and marked several heroes for Noxia's 6% maximum health follow-up.
Noxia's 20 ability haste brought Neural Disruptor back in about 70.8s instead of 85s, and Wraith Leggings added 12% magical damage on targets below 40% health.
Rimefang's stun and Winter's Pursuit's root on frostbitten targets set off Vortex Stone, cutting basic ability cooldowns by 20% and adding a shield before the next catch.
Basilisk 20, Earthshaker 15 and Vortex Stone 10 made 45 ability haste, bringing Frostfall back in about 62.1s instead of 90s for the next fight.
Melee heroes fill Earthshaker twice as fast, up to 10 stacks of 1.25% more ability damage, while Forticus shields Kaelen upon taking hero damage.
